kept.title: Arbitrary Code Execution via eval in File Parsing
kept.description: The `parseData` function in `lib/readFile.js` uses `eval` to process file contents if the extension is .js or .ts. An attacker who can influence the content of the translation files can execute arbitrary JavaScript code on the server.
steps_to_exploit: Attacker identifies a writable locale directory or gains access to the filesystem.
Attacker modifies or uploads a malicious .js file inside the locale folder.
Attacker triggers an application request that causes the i18next-fs-backend to read the malicious file.
The application executes `evalAlias(data)` on the malicious payload.
kept.impact: Full control over the Node.js or Deno process, leading to system compromise.

kept.title: Path Traversal via Unsafe `ns` Segment Handling
kept.description: While `lng` is validated against a strict set of rules, `ns` (namespace) is validated using `isSafeNsSegment` (a loose check), which allows directory traversals if the filesystem path is not strictly anchored to the expected base directory.
steps_to_exploit: Attacker crafts a namespace parameter containing directory traversal sequences (e.g., 'sub/../../etc/passwd').
The `interpolatePath` function allows the segment as it contains no restricted characters except `..` in a specific context.
The file read/write operations resolve the resulting path outside the target locale directory.
kept.impact: Unauthorized reading or overwriting of sensitive files on the server.

kept.title: Prototype Pollution in `defaults` Helper
kept.description: The `defaults` function in `lib/utils.js` attempts to block `__proto__`, `constructor`, and `prototype` in `UNSAFE_KEYS`, but it does not account for nested property access or other bypasses common in older JS environments, potentially leading to prototype pollution.
steps_to_exploit: Attacker provides a crafted object containing malicious deep properties that bypass the shallow `indexOf` check.
The `defaults` function merges these into the options object.
Application logic uses the tainted options object, causing unintended behavior or privilege escalation.
kept.impact: Global application state manipulation, potential denial of service or remote code execution.

kept.title: Insecure Script in `package.json` build command
kept.description: The build script in `example/fastify/package.json` executes `npm pack` and performs uncontrolled shell operations on untrusted archive contents, potentially leading to command injection during the build process.
steps_to_exploit: Attacker contributes a malicious package or modifies the package structure.
The CI/CD pipeline or a developer runs `npm run build`.
The script executes commands like `find ... -exec touch ...` and `tar -xvzf ...` in an unsafe manner.
kept.impact: Code execution on the build environment, leading to CI/CD pipeline compromise.

evidence.quote: "build": "rm -rf build && packageName=$(npm pack) && tar -xvzf $packageName && mv package build && rm $packageName && cd build && npm i --production && find ./node_modules/* -mtime +10950 -exec touch {} \\; && rm -f package-lock.json && cd

kept.title: Denial of Service via `expirationTime` File Deletion
kept.description: The backend automatically deletes files if they are expired. An attacker can force the backend to repeatedly attempt to remove files, causing disk I/O exhaustion or deleting legitimate files if the path can be manipulated.
steps_to_exploit: Attacker forces a high volume of requests for expired resources.
The application calls `removeFile` on the resulting paths.
Repeated file system writes and unlinks cause disk I/O load.
kept.impact: Denial of Service for legitimate users and potential file system instability.

kept.title: Path Traversal via `interpolatePath` with `+` separator
kept.description: The `interpolatePath` function supports `+` for joining segments, but if the underlying segment validator is bypassed (e.g., via loose `isSafeNsSegment`), the joined path can lead to directory traversal.
steps_to_exploit: Attacker uses a combined segment string with `+`.
Validator checks segments individually.
If one segment is unsafe but passes check, the result resolves to an arbitrary path.

kept.title: Insecure `eval` Alias Pattern
kept.description: The code creates an alias to `eval` using `const evalAlias = eval`. This is a classic pattern used to bypass some static analysis tools that look for direct `eval()` calls.
steps_to_exploit: Attacker exploits any existing data input that reaches the `parseData` switch case for .js/.ts files.
The `evalAlias(data)` call bypasses simple string-match security scanners.
kept.impact: Evasion of security tooling, facilitating successful code injection.

kept.title: Race Condition in Queued File Writes
kept.description: The `writeFile` method uses a simple boolean lock and a debounced function, but doesn't handle concurrent write requests to the same path effectively. It could lead to partial writes or corrupted JSON content if writes overlap.
steps_to_exploit: Attacker triggers multiple concurrent missing-key events.
Multiple `writeFile` calls are queued.
The file is read and written in a way that risks interleaving, resulting in corrupted JSON translations.
kept.impact: Denial of Service due to corrupted localization files.

kept.title: Lack of Content Security on `writeFile`
kept.description: The `writeFile` function does not validate the input payload for structural integrity beyond basic stringification. An attacker could potentially inject malicious structures into the JSON files.
steps_to_exploit: Attacker influences the `fallbackValue` used in `create()` or `save()`.
The application persists this value into the JSON file.
When the app re-reads the JSON file, the injected structure is parsed.
kept.impact: Stored cross-site scripting or application logic errors if the parsed JSON is used elsewhere.

kept.title: Use of `fs.readFileSync` in production code
kept.description: The code uses synchronous file operations (`fs.readFileSync`) when `initAsync` is false. This blocks the entire Node.js event loop while waiting for disk I/O.
steps_to_exploit: Attacker requests a resource that is not cached and forces a synchronous read.
The event loop is blocked, preventing the server from handling other requests.

kept.title: Exposure of sensitive info via verbose error messages
kept.description: Parsing errors explicitly include the filename in the error message, which may reveal directory structures to end users if passed back in API responses.
steps_to_exploit: Attacker provides malformed translation file.
Server responds with error message containing absolute server path.
kept.impact: Information disclosure of internal server structure.

kept.title: Weak validation in `isSafeSegmentBase`
kept.description: The length check (128 chars) and control character check are good but potentially insufficient. Other characters like shell metacharacters or specific OS-dependent path delimiters may still bypass validation depending on the host system.
steps_to_exploit: Attacker provides a segment containing unusual but technically allowed characters that may trigger non-standard behavior in the underlying OS path resolution.
kept.impact: Path traversal or unexpected filesystem behavior.

kept.title: Unsafe `module.exports` usage in CJS build
kept.description: The build process uses a fragile `fixcjs` regex replacement to patch internal require statements. This is highly error-prone and can lead to broken builds or security regressions.
steps_to_exploit: A dependency update changes the generated structure, causing the regex to replace the wrong part or nothing at all.
The application crashes or falls back to an insecure, non-bundled dependency.
kept.impact: Build instability and potential vulnerability to malicious dependency replacement.

kept.title: Reliance on `evalAlias` for `require`-like behavior
kept.description: The code tries to mimic CommonJS behavior in non-Node environments using `evalAlias`. Relying on eval for module loading logic is fundamentally insecure.
steps_to_exploit: An attacker compromises the translation data in a .js file, which is then loaded via the `evalAlias` evaluation loop.

kept.title: Insecure default directory permissions
kept.description: The library creates missing directories using `recursive: true` but does not enforce specific permissions, potentially inheriting default system permissions which may be too permissive.
steps_to_exploit: Attacker creates directories using the tool, then exploits the default permissions (e.g., world-writable) to replace translation files later.
kept.impact: Privilege escalation and unauthorized data modification.
